summary: Rejected. On the held-out checker batch AT (45 Java references, 42 Java-valid), the packet introduces 21 new valid-input errors, 5 lost whole-output matches and 2 lost rejections. On every other cohort (AS 54, AQ 43, 790, 28, retained 4,174, golden 12,550) it has no loss, and every broad gate holds.
findings: TIM ordering (obligation 1) is fixed: inactive, uninvoked and included sprite headers now behave as in Java. All 10 valid-input errors from the rejection now match, and AS (held out from the maker) has no loss.

LOSS (new valid-input errors, 17 Java-valid AT cases from mismatch to exit 1): the body of a multiline command that Rust handles after the sprite dispatch, or not at all, is offered to the sprite group. Java's CommonCommands#addCommonCommands1 calls addTitleCommands (CommandMultilinesTitle, CommandMultilinesLegend, CommandMultilinesHeader, CommandMultilinesFooter) before addCommonCommands2. The description CommandCreateElementMultilines and the legacy activity CommandMultilinesNoteActivity also own their bodies through END, so Java never offers a body line to getCandidate. Rust's component.rs, deployment.rs, usecase.rs and state.rs model only title, legend, note and skinparam bodies before dispatch; object.rs, and state legend/title bodies, reach the 'unrecognized' fallback; parse_legacy_activity dispatches every non-empty line. 'Sprite sheets are loaded' then becomes CommandSpriteFile and fails with 'Cannot read: are loaded', and 'Sprite frame {' fails with 'Cannot read: {'. Cases: ck_component_bracket_body, ck_component_bracket_lower, ck_deployment_node_bracket_body, ck_deployment_bracket_upper, ck_usecase_rectangle_bracket_body, ck_component_header_body, ck_component_footer_body, ck_deployment_header_body, ck_deployment_footer_upper, ck_state_header_body, ck_state_legend_body, ck_state_title_body, ck_object_header_body, ck_object_legend_body, ck_activity_legacy_note_body, ck_activity_legacy_note_brace, ck_activity_legacy_legend_body. This violates the account invariant ('bodies of multiline commands are never sprite commands') and 🎯T14.17's 'no valid case newly becomes an error'.

LOSS (4 lost matches that are now valid-input errors: ck_svg_body_apos_end_{legacy,teoz,class,component}): the old preprocessor handled sprite body lines before strip_inline_comment. Now the Rust-only trailing-apostrophe stripping (preprocess/mod.rs strip_inline_comment) reaches SVG body lines. Only the start line is exempt (SPRITE_SVG_START). '<text> 'hi'</text></svg>' is cut to '<text> ', so the CommandSpriteSvgMultiline END (.*</svg>)$ never matches and the command never completes. Java (StringLocated#removeInnerComment) strips only /' ... '/.

LOSS (2 lost rejections: ck_svg_body_trailing_after_end_{legacy,teoz}): by the same mechanism, '</svg> ' done' is stripped to '</svg> ', so END matches and an input Java rejects as a syntax error (END requires </svg> at end of line) is now accepted.

LOSS (1 lost match: ck_startsub_sprite_deployment; the control without !startsub, ck_nosub_sprite_deployment, still matches): a pixel sprite declared inside '!startsub … !endsub' in the same file. Java executes the startsub body in place, so the sprite is drawn. The old in-TIM collector registered it; Rust's TIM (preprocess/mod.rs, '!startsub' collecting_sub) does not emit the body to the diagram, so after the move the sprite is undefined and the node shrinks. The underlying cause is a TIM residue that the old collector masked; the packet exposes it as a lost match. The retained checker_dynamic_sub_sprite shows the same cause (sprite map lost; mismatch before and after).

Gains on AT: 3 class body cases (header, legend, floating note now keep 'Sprite…' text; mismatch to match). AQ: 27 gains (19 mismatches and 8 valid-input errors to match) and 4 newly rejected. AS: 9 gains and 15 newly rejected. The yaml and ditaa pass-through cases still mismatch for other reasons (yaml width 210 vs 207; ditaa is compare-101 in both builds).

Unclosed contracts: the AS cases confirm 'Cannot read: [2x2/16] {' for unclosed pixel headers and a syntax error for unclosed SVG headers in object, deployment, legacy activity, state and component. rejection_contract.py (unchanged) on 313 Java-invalid fresh inputs: 269 rejected before, 304 after, 0 lost; it exits 1 on 9 remaining false accepts (timing and mindmap fallback, compressed sprites, !function, cl_class_bare_sprite). The AT lost rejections are counted above; that script's manifest predates AT.

Cross-family: no golden changed except edge_render_sprite (a Java error page, now rejected): 1 of 12,550 SVG byte changes. Retained: 13 gains and 2 newly rejected, with no loss. Model changes are explained: the post-TIM source keeps sprite lines as Java's UmlSource does (about 50 golden and 30 retained), the sprite map loses inactive and body-owned entries, there are 7 HashMap-ordering changes, and the additive url_tooltip field is present.

Gates (each run once): golden_no_oracle failure names are byte-identical to 9834a7194 (70; 11,181/11,251). golden_pairs names are identical (754). parity_perturbations: 2,396 failures before, 2,366 after, 0 new. harness_guards: the same 2 failing guards; the decimal ratchet is byte-identical; review-record violations differ only by 2 'account has no independent checker review'. Workspace lib 1,486/1,486; pipe_mode 13/13. --yaml panics 148 golden and 63 retained in both builds; there are no SVG panics or timeouts.

Process: the account of record (ff761cd0a) planned to offer description/activity sprites last (as a known deviation); 95cf85252 offers them first, which is the Java order, without amending the account. The guard-schema account.json was added only in the evidence commit 5cf1eac12. Two earlier account files were edited for citation package names only.

Frozen items are unchanged: the rustuml-oracle crate (GEOM_EPS, syntax-error markers, census, allow-lists, strict-XML list), test-diagrams (golden pointer, baselines, ulp_parked) and the approved 15-entry new-valid-errors set. No production logic is keyed to fixture text, and there are no new decimal literals.
next_obligations: 1 (blocking): before the sprite dispatch, every family must own the bodies Java's earlier-registered multiline commands own: title, legend, header, footer and caption in all families, description '[ … ]' element bodies, legacy-activity note and legend bodies, and object and state legend/title bodies. The rule is ported from each factory's initCommandsList and addTitleCommands, not from fixture text. Perturbations: AT ck_*_body cases plus renamed text and other separators.

2 (blocking): no Rust-only comment stripping may apply to a line owned by an open sprite command. The exemption must cover the body and END lines of CommandSpriteSvgMultiline, which is the old ordering, or the trailing-apostrophe stripping must be removed where Java has none. Perturbations: ck_svg_body_apos_end_*, ck_svg_body_trailing_after_end_*.
3: emit '!startsub' bodies in place in the defining file (Java TIM). File this as its own TIM target if it is out of scope; it must not regress ck_startsub_sprite_deployment.
4: rerun AT, AS, AQ, 790 and 28 plus fresh renamed variants. Zero new valid-input errors, lost matches or lost rejections.
